summary: The reference patch implements every Schedule R (R-4) rule the instruction makes authoritative (carton receipt date, 40-cent return handling, at-or-above tiers on net purchases, half-up volume rebate, growth on the increase, 25,000-cent minimum), leaves unreached items (loose lines, tidy-up notices, price-match sales) on today's code with today's constants, and adds no guards; no concrete incorrect behavior found.
checks_performed: Reconciled all 27 manifest files against files read; every file read in full, none truncated.

Applied fix.patch hunks mentally against growth.py, ledger.py, rates.py, statement.py and tiers.py and checked hunk line ranges and counts against the shipped files (e.g. ledger -1,8 +1,15 adds 7 lines; tiers -1,6 +1,8 adds 2).

2.2/3.1/3.2: a line of units >= 12 is dated invoice + 4 days before the inclusive in_quarter test (fix.patch:31-32, dates.py:25-28); traced invoice first-4 -> first (counts), first-5 -> first-1 (excluded), last-3 -> last+1 (excluded); 11-unit lines keep the invoice date (no schedule rule reaches them).
3.3: return_charge now reads return_handling=40 (fix.patch:42,49), so credit = units*(unit_cents-40) = value - 40*units; claim_cutoff still reads unit_handling=25.
2.6/3.5: tier_rate uses >= and last matching row (fix.patch:84); thresholds strictly increasing so last match is highest reached; net < 0 matches no row (first threshold 0) and rate stays 0.
1.1/3.6: volume_rebate = half_up(net*bp, 10000); money.half_up (2n+d)//(2d) is nearest-with-half-up for n >= 0; for net < 0 bp is 0 so result 0.
4.1: prior <= 0 -> 0; net*100 < prior*110 -> 0; else half_up((net-prior)*200, 10000) with net-prior > 0; prior=1 needs net >= 2.
5.1: price drop (cut >= 250) with on_hand >= 100 gives credit >= 25,000 >= notice_cutoff 5,000, so the shipped cutoff never zeroes a price drop; tidy-ups keep today's 5,000 cutoff.
5.2: contract sale (below >= 100) always passes the shipped 25-cent claim cutoff and is below*units; non-contract sales keep today's code.

6.1/6.2: total is sum of four non-negative components; settle pays when total >= 25,000 (settlement_minimum now reads minimum_settlement=25000), else carries whole total; notice_cutoff still reads small_credit=5000.
Output: all values int (half_up and integer arithmetic), keys match README list, account order preserved by build_statements; rebate_run.py is not touched by the patch.

Cross-checked solution/model.py against the patched package rule by rule (counting_day, tier_rate, share, growth, price_credit, sale_chargeback, settle); they agree, and model.py mirrors shipped behaviour on unreached inputs.
Checked solve.sh runs patch -p1 from / with a/app/... paths and that patch is installed in environment/Dockerfile.
